result.topic_en: Calculation expressing the cosine and sine of half a complex argument f−ig in terms of auxiliary polar quantities a, A, b, B derived from cos(f−ig)=p+iq.
result.transcription:
Phys. 37 [-155 n. 4-]
(2)
$\cos(f-ig) = p+iq$
$1+p = a\cos A$ $\quad 1-p = b\cos B$
$q = a\sin A$ $\quad q = b\sin B$
$\frac{a-b}{2} = \cos f$
$\frac{a+b}{2} = \cos ig$
1 $\sqrt{\frac{a}{2}}\,(\cos\tfrac12 A + i\sin\tfrac12 A) = \cos\tfrac12(f-ig)$
2 $\sqrt{\frac{a}{2}}\,(\cos\tfrac12 A - i\sin\tfrac12 A) = \cos\tfrac12(f+ig)$
3 $\sqrt{\frac{b}{2}}\,(\cos\tfrac12 B - i\sin\tfrac12 B) = \sin\tfrac12(f-ig)$
4 $\sqrt{\frac{b}{2}}\,(\cos\tfrac12 B + i\sin\tfrac12 B) = \sin\tfrac12(f+ig)$
$1.4 = \sqrt{ab}\cos\tfrac12(A+B) = \sin f$ [?]
$\tfrac12$[?] 2.3
[-$i\sqrt{ab}\sin\tfrac12(A+B)$-] $= \cos$ :
$\sqrt{ab}\cos\tfrac12(A+B) = \sin f$
$i\sqrt{ab}\,[-\cos-]\sin\tfrac12(A+B) = \sin ig$
